### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 68 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2548ba57deb83062cc94ea91a644309092251a0f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1969643772a66fcd0db81d7797b7b982af14c2ec` — the merge of head `8b5c2cee52238d338430665e508ecdd205a31e43` into base `2548ba57deb83062cc94ea91a644309092251a0f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1969643772a66fcd0db81d7797b7b982af14c2ec && git checkout 1969643772a66fcd0db81d7797b7b982af14c2ec
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2548ba57deb83062cc94ea91a644309092251a0f 8b5c2cee52238d338430665e508ecdd205a31e43 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2548ba57deb83062cc94ea91a644309092251a0f && git merge --no-ff 8b5c2cee52238d338430665e508ecdd205a31e43

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2548ba57deb83062cc94ea91a644309092251a0f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `26421788b475f8dd6336158c551ad3a2ce1008d6`

Reviewed head = branch head = PR head (no drift). Merge-base `afc3b64928`; 5 files, +617/−30, exactly the declared surface (`engine.ts`, `integrity/dangling-reference-audit.ts`, two test files, the changeset).

### ① Derived judgments

- (a) FALSE under `group`. The changeset's "One case to check" says a detail record pointing at a header in another organization "now edits as if its header were missing … The dangling-reference audit below now reports such records". At head, `inspectDanglingReferences` computes `unionScope = postureUsesUnionScope(this.resolveEnginePosture())` and, when true, hands `referenceExists` no context, so a header that exists in any organization resolves. Under `group` those records are exactly the declared blind spot: NOT reported. The sentence carries no posture qualifier; the title line ("…and the dangling-reference audit reports cross-organization references") has the same defect. The paragraph's first sentence is also over-broad under `group`: leg 1 spreads the caller context, so a header inside the editor's `accessible_org_ids` still binds. Consumer-facing changeset prose false in a posture: defect, fix in ③-2.
- (b) ACCURATE. The `group` blind spot in the docblock is correct and never stricter than the guard: `buildDriverOptions` widens to `tenantIds` only on an injected `'group'` provider with a non-empty `accessible_org_ids`, else equality. Minor incompleteness: the parenthetical omits writes made before #19808's guard existed.
- (c) TRUE. `carriesOrganization` rejects `undefined`, `null` and `''`, so the port passes no context and no `tenantId` reaches the driver; same for `tenancy.enabled: false` and a federated phantom column. Pinned in both test files.
- (d) TRUE. `probe(target, id, organization?: string | null)`: a two-parameter implementer stays assignable, a two-argument call stays valid, and an implementer ignoring the argument behaves as before. The two pre-existing in-repo ports are untouched and `Test Core` is green.
- (e) TRUE by construction, unpinned. All parent-binding sites and all `assertReferencesResolve` doors pass `opCtx.context` through `referenceCheckContext` → `find`/`findOne` → `buildDriverOptions`, the single place `tenantIds` is set, so a group member binds a header in any organization of their membership set. No leg-1 case runs under `group` (③-6).
- Test names, docblocks and the remaining changeset statements (platform-global / federated / NULL-organization headers still bind; RLS still ignored; the audit runs with the lifecycle sweep) are true at head. The `resolveMasterDetailParent` docblock omits the `group` union (③-4).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch` with `Clause-②: no` HOLDS. `DanglingReferenceAuditPort` is exported, and `?organization` is a type-level widening of one signature. But clause ② is about what consumers can hand the package; this is an OUTBOUND datum the audit hands to a port it calls. It adds no authorable key, no accepted payload key, no export and no error code, and the class is the #19800 tenant-isolation restoration precedent. `Check Changeset` is green on the current pair.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. Posture-read divergence (dev-noted): ACCEPTABLE for this PR. The audit keys on `resolveEnginePosture()`; `buildDriverOptions` widens only on a raw injected `'group'`. The divergent cell (no provider, env `group`) under-reports relative to the guard: less strict, never stricter, read-only, no exposure, in a configuration ADR-0105 D12 does not entitle.
2. Changeset prose false under `group` (① a): MUST FIX BEFORE LANDING, prose only. Qualify the title line and the "One case to check" audit sentence with "outside the `group` posture", and say a header outside the caller's tenant scope (under `group`, outside their membership set) is treated as absent.
3. Stale PR-body statements (the seat edits them; not verdict input): the "Open question" section, Leg 2's missing union exception, the Tests line on the `group` pin, A3's "Leg 2 now reports exactly these rows", ablation leg 2 and local verification cited at `5930c9898a`, A4's unstated harness posture (`isolated`), and Deviations omitting the `postureUsesUnionScope` import.
4. `resolveMasterDetailParent` docblock omits the `group` union: ACCEPTABLE; fold into the fix commit.
5. Blind-spot parenthetical omits writes before #19808: ACCEPTABLE.
6. No leg-1 pin under `group`: ACCEPTABLE; add in the fix round.
7. Under `group` the probe memo stays keyed per organization while the engine ignores it: perf only, ACCEPTABLE.
8. Checks at review time: 32 of 33 latest-per-name `success` or `skipped`; `Type Check · workspace` still `in_progress`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-19837-parent-binding-tenant-scope`
Reviewed-by: `session_01TEhopqrWQYBycZzyJHpAZr`

**VERDICT: FAIL**: defect ① (a). The changeset's "One case to check" paragraph and title line assert an unqualified audit report that is false under the `group` posture at head. The minimal fix is ③-2, a prose-only changeset edit. A patch round is in flight; a fresh review runs on its head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8b5c2cee52238d338430665e508ecdd205a31e43`

Reviewed head = branch head = PR head (no drift). Merge-base `afc3b64928`; 5 files, +645/−30, exactly the declared surface. `main`'s only `engine.ts` drift since the merge-base is three hunks in `reportFindFailure` (#19840), disjoint from every region this PR edits. Since the FAILed head `26421788b4` (record 5794714685), the diff is changeset prose, `engine.ts` docblocks only (no non-comment line changed), and one new test. The earlier defect is gone: the title line and the "One case to check" paragraph are posture-qualified.

### ① Derived judgments

- (a) Title line. The audit half is TRUE in every posture: `postureUsesUnionScope` is `posture === 'group'`, so `single` and `isolated` probe under the row's organization and only `group` stays unscoped. The leg-1 shorthand ("another organization's header") is defined by the body's own parenthetical (under `group`, outside the caller's membership set). TRUE.
- (b) "One case to check": TRUE. Outside `group` the probe runs under the detail row's organization and the other organization's header is not found, so the record is reported. Under `group` the probe is unscoped and the header resolves, so it is not reported, exactly as the paragraph now says.
- (c) Leg-1 sentence on headers outside the caller's scope: TRUE at every door. Both resolvers read under `referenceCheckContext(context)` = `{ ...context, isSystem: true }`. `buildDriverOptions` forwards `tenantId`, and adds `tenantIds` only on an injected `'group'` provider with a non-empty `accessible_org_ids`. The exemptions hold as stated: `tenancy.enabled: false`, federated, NULL-organization, RLS bypass, and a system caller with no `tenantId`. All five call sites pass `opCtx.context`.
- (d) Audit paragraph: TRUE in all four cells (NULL organization, empty stamp, tenancy-disabled and federated phantom all probe unscoped; the memo key cannot collide). "Implementations that ignore it keep working": TRUE. `probe(target, id, organization?: string | null)` keeps two-parameter implementers assignable; the two pre-existing in-repo ports are untouched and every Type Check gate is green.
- (e) New `group` leg-1 test: meaningful. The positive half separates union from equality (`note` `required`, plus `tenantIds` on the single header `find`; the recorded ablation received `[]`). The org-X-only lit control answers `header` `reference_not_found` and would also red under the bare read.
- (f) Audit `group` test: meaningful. No `rts_account` probe carries a `tenantId`, and the same rows re-run under `isolated` are reported.
- (g) Docblocks and test names: TRUE. The PR body is true except "9 cases" for the leg-1 describe, which now has 10.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql: patch` with `Clause-②: no` HOLDS. The diff adds no export (`DanglingReferenceAuditPort` was already exported), no authorable or accepted key, no error code, and no public signature change on `ObjectQL`. The only type-level change is an OPTIONAL third parameter on a port the package CALLS: an outbound datum, not a widened accept set. The class is a tenant-isolation restoration, as PR #19800 was. `Check Changeset` and `check-changeset-no-major` are green.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. Posture-read divergence: ACCEPTABLE. Every cell was walked (provider `'group'`, env-only `group`, an unnormalised provider value, a throwing env). There is no cell where the audit is stricter than the guard; the less-strict cells are read-only and sit in a lean embedding with no Layer 0 wall above the driver.
2. `DanglingReferenceAuditPort.probe` docblock ("The engine probes under that organization") lacks the `group` qualifier: ACCEPTABLE. The deciding site states the exception, and a custom port replaces the engine's.
3. Title-line leg-1 shorthand under `group`: ACCEPTABLE, defined two sentences later.
4. NULL-organization detail row in "One case to check": ACCEPTABLE; the audit paragraph states that rule.
5. PR body "9 cases" (10 at head): ACCEPTABLE, not consumer-facing.
6. `Test Core (1/6)` red at review time: `@objectstack/spec` `error-catalog-docs.test.ts` threw `ENOENT … packages/spec/tsup.config.bundled_*.mjs` from `walk()` in `scripts/check-error-status-conformance.mjs`, a readdir-then-stat race with a concurrent tsup build. Neither file is in this diff, and the same shard was green on `26421788b4`. NOT a defect of the diff; one re-run is required before landing.
7. The unreleased #19808 changeset on `main` says the audit "still checks existence across all organizations". In the same release as this changeset, the pair reads as a contradiction to an upgrader. OPTIONAL, docs-only, outside this PR's surface.
8. Under `group` the memo stays keyed per organization while the probe is unscoped: perf only, ACCEPTABLE.
9. `single` posture with explicitly stamped rows from writers carrying no `tenantId`: the audit probes them scoped while their writes were checked unscoped. Not claimed anywhere: ACCEPTABLE.
